# Validation performed for version 1.0.1

All 22 tests pass: the original 17 below and five regression cases for the returned-run failures. The new cases force 28 physical fragments across four chooser buckets and compare complete histories and fixed-effect moments against a single-table reference; reconstruct saved partial residual summaries without changing their source and compare exact raw/adjusted account counts; reject duplicate account cells even when their counts match; exercise the original S0 timestamp boundary without an F50 flag; and verify conditional-logit invariance to million-fold changes in regressor units and exact Newton stationarity.

The full synthetic integration was rerun successfully for v1.0.1. These tests verify the correction and checkpoint reuse on synthetic files; the repaired 41.5-million-row analysis still needs to run on the user's Mac. The v1.0.0 synthetic fixture did not force multiple physical files per bucket and therefore missed the production fragmentation error. Its old B outputs are not validated by the old synthetic pass.

Seventeen numerical and contract tests pass. They check source projection and both-role author exclusion; exact C/N/L boundaries; missing opportunities versus zero grants; literal-resample Spearman ranks; jointly bootstrapped matrix contrasts and deterministic seeding; no P2 leakage into P1 classification; within-chooser OLS against explicit chooser dummies; group-specific stage design rank; exact conditional-logit likelihood, score, Hessian and parameter recovery; gamma–Poisson probabilities, analytic mixture gradients and the Poisson boundary; strictly earlier, mutually exclusive receipt histories; joint 2SLS against a direct matrix calculation; weighted receipt fixed effects against explicit WLS; and checkpoint rejection after input/report changes.

A separate end-to-end synthetic run passes with 160 accounts, 15,360 opportunities, two years and both states. It exercises account aggregation/partitioning, raw and adjusted persistence, nuisance fitting/scoring, bootstrap tables, six B models, both B profile panels, the D trigger/provisional fit, C likelihoods/forecast/figure, first-future-choice SQL, aggregate export-column checks and readout generation. The synthetic integration uses 29 bootstrap draws to test plumbing; production requires exactly 999. Numerical bootstrap checks also compare literal resampling and use separate seeded simulations.

The integration simulates interruption after score checkpoints are saved but before the adjustment parent is certified. Resume verifies and retains the existing nuisance-fit file, preserves its identity, reuses score checkpoints and completes the parent. Completed raw persistence is reused with identical status. Independent worker outputs are reduced in input order.

The plotting code is unchanged from the earlier visually inspected B and C outputs. Empty/nonidentified profile support is labeled rather than displayed as an estimated flat line. Shell launchers pass bash syntax checks, Python sources compile, and the package has an integrity manifest. Aggregate report directories are explicitly allowlisted for export; row identifiers and game/account names are absent from synthetic output-table schemas.

The original 41.5-million-row data, August profiles and completed R7 private inputs are on the user's Mac and were not available in this workspace. Full-sample reproduction gates, A/A3 estimates, matched-receipt source binding and IV source binding must therefore execute there. No new empirical coefficient, mechanism conclusion, full-scale runtime, peak RAM usage or completed Mac run is claimed by these tests. The underlying estimators are verified synthetically and the adapters are bound to recovered producer code and archived source identities. The setup script's optional package installation was not run against the user's environment.

Test logs and the runtime versions used for validation are in `validation/`. Synthetic fixtures and outputs are not evidence about Lichess behavior.
